title: Come Happy Souls, Approach Your God
description: Come Happy Souls, Approach Your God in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 103, headed “Christ's commission, John 3. 16 17”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come hap-py souls, ap-proach your God With new me-lo-dious songs; Come, ren-der to al-might-y grace The tri-bute of your tongues.

lines: Come happy souls, approach your God
So strange, so boundless was the love
The Father sent his equal Son
Thy hands, dear Jesus, were not arm'd
But all was mercy, all was mild,
When Christ on the kind errand came,
Here, sinners, you may heal your wounds,
Trust in the mighty Saviour's Name,
See, dearest Lord our willing souls
We bless the great Redeemer's love,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
